procedure: Take a strip of paper and draw a straight line along its length.
Using a ruler, mark centimetre divisions along the line and label them 0, 1, 2, 3, and so on.
For the first scale, divide each centimetre into 5 equal parts and draw small marks at the divisions.
For the second scale, divide each centimetre into 2 equal parts and draw small marks at the divisions.
Label the scales to show their least counts.
aim: To make paper scales having least counts of 0.2 cm and 0.5 cm.

viva.question: What is the least count of an instrument?
viva.answer: It is the smallest measurement that the instrument can read.

viva.question: How many equal parts are there in 1 cm on the 0.2 cm scale?
How many equal parts are there in 1 cm on the 0.5 cm scale?

calculation: For the first scale: least count = 1 cm ÷ 5 = 0.2 cm = 2 mm.
For the second scale: least count = 1 cm ÷ 2 = 0.5 cm = 5 mm.
diagram: Draw two straight paper scales, each marked in centimetres from 0 onwards; show each centimetre divided into five equal parts on the first scale and two equal parts on the second, and label them “Least count = 0.2 cm” and “Least count = 0.5 cm”.
title: Making paper scales of different least counts
precautions: Draw the scale line straight and keep the paper flat.
Make all subdivisions equal in length.
Use a sharp pencil to make fine, clear marks.
Label the centimetre marks and least counts clearly.
result: Two paper scales were made: one with a least count of 0.2 cm (2 mm) and the other with a least count of 0.5 cm (5 mm).
